messages:
maya: Quick sanity run of the handshake-prefetch patch on llama4t-13b-q4. Deployed a canary to the dedicated pool and ran ~1k prompts against our smoke harness. Initial notes:
- p50 per-token latency down ~28%
- throughput up ~22% under identical tail-SLOs
- seeing a small quality blip on long-context generative tasks

oliver: Nice. Can you paste the config + perf numbers so we can triage?

maya: config used for the run:
```
handshake_prefetch: true
prefetch_window: 32
batch_size: 8
quant: q4_0
seed: 42
```
Perf (p50 token latency): baseline 45 ms -> patch 32 ms
Throughput: baseline 1.0x -> 1.22x at same concurrency

sasha: Quick-quality check on a 500-case eval subset (mix of MMLU-like probes + summarization):
- MMLU-proxy acc: 75.4 -> 74.9 (-0.5)
- Rouge-L (summarization subset): 0.430 -> 0.418 (-0.012)
- Perplexity (held-out): 10.2 -> 10.5
Regression concentrated on prompts with >2k tokens and multi-turn coherence. Could be token boundary effects. :thinking:

jonah: Do we have KV-cache telemetry? evictions/hits? Also any obvious sampling noise (seeded runs)?

maya: KV stats summary: hit-rate improved +3.5% overall, but we observe intermittent eviction collisions when a prefetch window overlaps a tile boundary. Small log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T12:34:01Z] prefetched: seq 0-31 -> ok
[2026-03-18T12:34:01Z] prefetch: seq 32-63 -> eviction collision at slot 31
[2026-03-18T12:34:01Z] fallback: synchronous fetch -> +4 ms
```
So mostly win, but rare collisions add latency and may trigger slightly different token probabilities on long contexts.

sasha: Sounds like a race when prefetch_window aligns with our tile boundaries. Quick mitigations to try:
- increase prefetch_window to 48 (reduces overlap frequency)
- add a cheap boundary-check to avoid overlapping evictions (cheap mutex per tile)
- run with deterministic seeds for sampling to rule out randomness

maya: Will run q4 + prefetch_window=48 + seed fixed. Re-running the 500-case eval and a 2k-token stress subset, will post numbers in ~2 hrs. deploy-bot: canary status?

deploy-bot: Canary deployed to pool-ml-dedicated-3, health checks passed, traffic at 5% :rocket:

oliver: If regressions persist after the boundary tweak, try disabling handshake_prefetch and instead increase batching (batch_size=12) to chase latency without introducing prefetch churn. Also capture diffs on top-k token distributions for the long-context cases.

maya: Good plan. Updating run plan now and will DM detailed run artifacts (logs + eval csv).
